meta.title_plain: How a bug-collecting kid created Pokémon
meta.teaser: Satoshi Tajiri turned his childhood love of catching bugs into Pokémon.

page.title: How a bug-collecting kid created Pokémon
page.bigIdea: Satoshi Tajiri mixed two things he loved as a kid, bugs and games. That mix became one of the biggest game series ever.

cards.title: The kid called Dr. Bug
cards.front: Satoshi was born in 1965 in Tokyo, Japan. He grew up near rice fields and rivers.
cards.back: He loved catching insects so much that other kids called him "Dr. Bug". He even invented his own trick: beetles slept under stones he left by trees.
cards.tryit: Go outside for 10 minutes and count how many different bugs you can spot.

cards.title: From ponds to arcades
cards.front: As the city grew, trees were cut down and the bugs disappeared.
cards.back: A fishing pond near his home became an arcade. Satoshi fell in love with Space Invaders and started thinking about how games were made.
cards.tryit: Play a game you love and write down one thing that makes it fun.

cards.title: A handmade game magazine
cards.front: As a teenager, Satoshi made his own magazine called Game Freak.
cards.back: It was handwritten and stapled together, full of tips to win games. Artist Ken Sugimori joined him. In 1989 they turned it into a game company.
cards.tryit: Write a one-page tips sheet for a game you're good at, like Brawl Stars.

cards.title: The idea in a cable
cards.front: In 1990 Satoshi saw a cable that linked two Game Boys together.
cards.back: He imagined bugs crawling from one Game Boy to the other. That sparked the idea: catch creatures, then trade them with friends.
cards.tryit: Think of two hobbies you love. Sketch a game idea that mixes them.

cards.title: Six years of not quitting
cards.front: Pokémon Red and Green took six years to make.
cards.back: Money ran so low that some workers quit, and Satoshi took no pay. The games finally came out in 1996 and became a huge hit.
cards.tryit: Pick one tough skill. Practise it 15 minutes a day this week, even when it's boring.

words.d: A homemade magazine made by fans about something they love.
A wire that connects two game consoles so they can share data.
The person who plans how a game works and what makes it fun.
An experienced person who guides and teaches someone newer.

quiz.q: What did other kids call young Satoshi?
quiz.hint: Think about his favourite hobby before video games.
quiz.why: He caught so many insects that kids nicknamed him Dr. Bug.

quiz.q: What gave Satoshi the big idea for trading Pokémon?
opts: A cable linking two Game Boys
quiz.hint: Look at card 4. Something had to connect two players.
quiz.why: He imagined bugs moving through the link cable between two Game Boys.

quiz.q: What was Game Freak before it was a game company?
quiz.hint: Satoshi stapled the pages together himself.
quiz.why: Game Freak started as his handwritten tips magazine, then became a studio in 1989.

quiz.q: Why does the Pokémon story show the power of not giving up?
opts: It was finished in one month
It took six years and almost ran out of money
quiz.hint: Read card 5 about how long it took.
quiz.why: Satoshi kept going for six years, even working without pay, until it was done.

page.think: Satoshi turned his favourite childhood hobby into a game. If you made a game from something you love, like tennis or anime, what would players collect or do?
